name: scratch-pad
title: Scratch Pad
description: A conceptual net-skill: 8 neurons grafted all-to-all into the live mesh, modeling a two-option draft loop wired toward the zip loop's send path. Option one is edit -- revise the draft in place, including writing or editing a numbered tool-comment to track progress through a repeated task (e.g. step 1, 2, 3 of 400); neither counts as sending. Option two is verify then send -- check the draft, then commit it as real output through send-to-zip-loop, the only path out of the scratch pad. Tool-comments never connect to send-to-zip-loop, so they never travel with what actually gets sent. Like every net-skill in this architecture, this is a real, hand-built connectionist scaffold (not executable code): install it and its neurons compute alongside the rest of the mesh from the first tick, the same all-to-all equation as everything already there, and continue learning with it. See scratch-pad.source.json for the NeuroLang source this compiles from, and net-skill-graft.ts for how a mesh grows one.
